newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 11.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5649. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- If Hong In-gil and Chung Jae-chull, members of parliament from the ruling New Korea Party, are found to have used influence to provide preferential loans to Hanbo Steel Co, arrest warrants would be sought against them on Tuesday, state prosecutors said.

- The Ministry of Finance and Economy expects South Korea's unemployment rate to rise to 2.5 percent in the first quarter of this year from 1.8 percent in October 1996. The total number of people unemployed rose to nearly 530,000 in January from 479,000 last December.

- Kwon Roh-kap, a leading member of the main opposition National Congress for New Politics who was summoned by prosecutors in connection with loans to Hanbo Steel, apologised on Monday for accepting political funds from the company and causing public concern.
- The government has decided to provide massive funds to help relieve a credit crunch among small- and medium-sized companies .
